questions: What is inside and outside the semiconductor industry, and where are boundaries ambiguous?
What are the stages of the value chain and which participant types operate in each?
How does money flow between participant types, and which business models exist?

status_note: Discovery pass: 6 lenses merged; claims await fact-check
title: Discovery: what is the semiconductor industry, who is in it, and how does it fit together
why_it_matters: Nothing else can be planned until we know the industry's boundaries, segments, participant types, flows and rule-makers from evidence rather than assumption.

questions: How exactly do WSTS, Gartner, Omdia, TechInsights and IDC define and compute the semiconductor market?
How are foundry revenue, captive/custom chips, distribution resale and memory price swings treated?
Why did Gartner's 2024 estimate move from US$626bn to US$655.9bn?
title: Market-sizing methodology: WSTS vs Gartner vs other publishers
why_it_matters: Headline market size differs by publisher and vintage; the atlas must state which population each number measures.

primary_sources: TSMC, UMC, GlobalFoundries, SMIC annual reports
questions: What are the pure-play, total foundry and Foundry 2.0 market sizes 2020-2025?
Who are the top foundries and their shares under each definition?
title: Foundry market: definitions (pure-play vs Foundry 2.0), size and shares
why_it_matters: Foundry is the core manufacturing layer for fabless firms and its size depends heavily on definition.

questions: What are SEMI's 22+ equipment segments and their sizes?
How do front-end vs back-end equipment and new vs refurbished equipment differ?
title: Semiconductor manufacturing equipment: segments, size and geography
why_it_matters: Equipment is a separately measured US$135bn market whose segmentation (lithography, deposition, etch, test, etc.) is not yet mapped.

questions: What are the SEMI materials sub-segments and sizes?
Which materials are most geographically concentrated?
title: Semiconductor materials: segments and suppliers
why_it_matters: US$73bn materials market (wafers, photoresist, gases, substrates) is a separate layer with its own concentration risks.

questions: What is the annual ESD market and its categories?
Which firms dominate EDA and IP licensing?
title: EDA and semiconductor IP market
why_it_matters: EDA/IP is small in revenue but a critical chokepoint; ESD Alliance measures it separately.

questions: How large is the OSAT market and who leads it?
How is advanced packaging defined and measured?
title: Assembly, test and advanced packaging (OSAT and in-house)
why_it_matters: Back-end is measured inconsistently (OSAT revenue vs Foundry 2.0 vs equipment) and advanced packaging is central to AI chips.

questions: What are the exact WSTS end-use shares for 2023-2025?
How much of 2025-2026 growth is price vs volume, and AI vs other?
title: End-market segmentation and the 2025-2026 AI/memory surge
why_it_matters: WSTS forecasts 90% growth in 2026 driven by memory; end-use shares are shifting fast towards computing/AI.

questions: What do US NAICS 334413 and 333242, NACE 26.11 and HS 8541/8542/8486 cover exactly?
Which official datasets are usable for size, employment and trade, and with what caveats?
title: Official statistics mapping: NAICS, ISIC/NACE, HS codes and their limits
why_it_matters: Government data (production, employment, trade) use broader classifications than industry bodies; the atlas needs a crosswalk.

questions: Which adjacent industries share processes, equipment or classifications with semiconductors?
How large are they and should any be in scope?
title: Boundary industries: displays, solar PV, passive components, PCBs and EMS
why_it_matters: These use semiconductor-like processes or share classifications but are excluded from the semiconductor market; scope decisions must be explicit.

primary_sources: Company 10-K/20-F filings (TSMC, UMC, AMD, Qualcomm, Nvidia, ASE)
questions: How did the revenue share of fabless firms, foundries and IDMs evolve from 1990 to 2025?
When and why did assembly/test (OSAT) move offshore and become independent?
Which IDMs went fab-lite or fabless, when and why?
secondary_sources: academic histories of the foundry model
title: History: the disaggregation of the value chain (IDM to fabless/foundry/OSAT/IP), 1980-2025
why_it_matters: The split into fabless, foundry, OSAT, EDA and IP specialists is the single biggest structural change in who captures value; this pass found dated milestones but no quantified share series.

questions: What is the DRAM and NAND revenue/price time series by year?
How did the number of DRAM makers fall over time, and via which bankruptcies/mergers?
What role did HBM and AI play in the 2024-2025 upswing?
title: History: memory cycles and memory-maker consolidation (1970-2025)
why_it_matters: Memory has repeatedly caused industry-wide crises (1985, 2001, 2008, 2012 Elpida, 2023) and consolidated to a few firms; understanding the cycle is essential to any capacity or pricing judgement.

questions: What did each US BIS rule (2019 Huawei, Oct 2022, Oct 2023, Dec 2024, 2025-26 changes) control?
What did the Netherlands and Japan add, and when?
What countermeasures did China adopt (e.g. critical mineral export controls)?
title: Policy: evolution of semiconductor export controls 2018-2026 (US, Netherlands, Japan, China countermeasures)
why_it_matters: Export controls now shape who can sell equipment and advanced chips to whom; the regime changed repeatedly after 2019 and includes Chinese countermeasures.

primary_sources: European Commission / European Court of Auditors
questions: What was appropriated vs actually disbursed in each regime?
Which fabs were funded and what is their status?
How did US policy change in 2025 (equity stakes, Section 232)?
title: Policy: comparison of chip industrial policies (US CHIPS, EU Chips Act, Japan, Korea, China, Taiwan, India)
why_it_matters: The post-2020 policy turn directs hundreds of billions in subsidies; results and disbursement differ widely from announced totals.

questions: What were Japan's shares of the total market by year and product?
What were the VLSI Project and later consolidation (Elpida, Renesas, Kioxia) and why did share fall?
title: History: Japan's rise and decline in semiconductors (1970s-2010s)
why_it_matters: Japan's rise triggered the first trade war and industrial-policy response; its decline shows how leadership shifts. This pass lacked primary share data.

primary_sources: Nvidia/AMD/Broadcom/TSMC/SK hynix/Micron filings and earnings transcripts
questions: How large is AI-related semiconductor revenue and which segments capture it?
What bottlenecks (CoWoS packaging, HBM) emerged and who controls them?
How does this compare historically with PC and smartphone demand waves?
title: Dynamics: the AI demand shift - accelerators, HBM and advanced packaging (2022-2026)
why_it_matters: AI data-center demand has become the dominant growth driver and shifted value toward GPU/accelerator designers, leading-edge foundry, HBM memory and advanced packaging.

primary_sources: TSMC, UMC, GlobalFoundries, SMIC 20-F/annual report notes on contract liabilities and temporary receipts
questions: How are foundry wafers priced by node and what drives price changes?
What prepayment, capacity-reservation and shortfall terms are used, and how large are they (contract liabilities)?
How were LTAs renegotiated in 2023-2024?
title: Foundry commercial terms: wafer pricing, LTAs and capacity prepayments
why_it_matters: The fabless-to-foundry payment is the largest design-to-manufacturing money flow; pricing basis and risk-sharing terms were not established in discovery.

primary_sources: Micron, SK hynix, Samsung, Kioxia annual reports
questions: How are DRAM/NAND priced (contract vs spot) and how often renegotiated?
How do inventory write-downs and utilisation cuts transmit the cycle to profits and capex?
What is HBM's pricing and contracting model?
title: Memory business model and price cycle
why_it_matters: Memory is the most cyclical segment (2023 fall ~29-37%, 2025 rise ~35%); contract vs spot pricing and inventory behaviour drive industry cyclicality.

primary_sources: Avnet, Arrow, WPG, WT Microelectronics 10-K/annual reports
Chipmaker 10-K revenue recognition notes (TI, Microchip, ADI, NXP)

What are distributor gross/operating margins on semiconductors?
title: Distribution channel economics
why_it_matters: Distributors hold inventory and are protected by suppliers; mechanics (ship-and-debit, price protection, stock rotation) and margins not established.

entities: China National IC Industry Investment Fund
primary_sources: METI, MOTIE, MIIT/Big Fund disclosures, India Semiconductor Mission, EU Chips Act state-aid decisions

title: Government money flows into semiconductors by country
why_it_matters: Subsidies, tax credits and state equity now co-fund fabs; only US and EU/Germany flows were captured in discovery.

How much advanced packaging revenue is captured by foundries versus OSATs?
What capex does advanced packaging require?
title: Packaging and test value pool, incl. advanced packaging

title: Cross-model financial benchmark (margins, capex, R&D) on consistent periods
why_it_matters: Discovery gathered single-company figures across mismatched fiscal years; a consistent benchmark by business model is needed before generalising.

How does the 48D credit work and will its 2026 deadline change?
What guardrail conditions bind recipients?

What rate will the Section 301 action reach in June 2027?
How do tariff offset programmes work?
title: US tariffs and trade remedies on semiconductors (Section 232, Section 301, reciprocal tariffs)
why_it_matters: Tariffs change landed cost of chips and derived electronics and are being used to force onshoring.

questions: What does Regulation 2023/1781 require and fund, article by article?

Which State aid decisions were approved, for whom and how much?
When does the 2026 dual-use list update and revised FDI regulation apply?
title: EU semiconductor regime: Chips Act, Chips Act 2.0, State aid, dual-use controls and FDI screening
why_it_matters: Defines subsidy eligibility and export/investment constraints for Europe's equipment and chip makers.

questions: Which items do Dutch, Japanese and Taiwanese controls cover and how are they licensed?
How aligned are they with US rules?
What has Taiwan done to protect core technologies (N-1 rules, core key technology list)?
title: Allied export controls: Netherlands, Japan, Taiwan, South Korea and the Wassenaar Arrangement
why_it_matters: Most leading-edge equipment comes from the Netherlands and Japan; their national controls decide what reaches China.

questions: What are all MOFCOM export controls touching semiconductor inputs, and their suspension status?
How large and how deployed are Big Fund I-III?
What happened to the analog IC anti-dumping probe?
What other levers (Unreliable Entity List, CAC reviews, procurement rules) are used?
title: China's semiconductor policy toolkit: Big Fund, critical-mineral export controls, Unreliable Entity List, trade remedies, cybersecurity review
why_it_matters: China is both the largest target of controls and an increasingly active rule-maker whose measures hit materials supply and US firms.

questions: What are the legal instruments, budgets and disbursements in each country?
Has Korea's Semiconductor Special Act entered into force and with which decrees?
Which projects did India approve under ISM and ISM 2.0?
title: Asian industrial policy: Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and India incentive programmes
why_it_matters: Subsidy and tax design decides where new fabs, packaging plants and design centres locate.

questions: What does the EU universal PFAS restriction propose for semiconductor uses and on what timeline?
How does Regulation 2024/573 treat semiconductor manufacturing gases?
Which US EPA rules (TSCA PFAS reporting) affect fabs?
title: Environmental, chemical and disclosure rules affecting fabs (PFAS, F-gases, water, conflict minerals, RoHS)
why_it_matters: Fabs depend on fluorinated chemicals and gases; restrictions could force costly substitution. Public evidence was thin in discovery.

questions: Which bodies set which standards, and who participates?
Which standards are de facto mandatory for market access (e.g. AEC-Q100 for automotive)?
title: Technical standards bodies for semiconductors (SEMI, JEDEC, IEC TC47, AEC, ISO/IEEE)
why_it_matters: Standards govern interoperability of equipment, memory interfaces and automotive qualification; they shape market access.

questions: What does a leading-edge PDK contain and how is access governed?
How do EDA vendors, IP vendors and foundries certify flows and IP for a node?
What exactly is handed over at tape-out (GDSII/OASIS, mask ordering data) and to whom?
How are multi-project wafers/shuttles organized?
title: Design enablement and design-data handoff: EDA, IP, PDKs, tape-out and mask data
why_it_matters: Design is ~half of industry value added and every chip passes through a foundry PDK, EDA flow and tape-out; this is the main information interface between designers and manufacturers.

questions: Which systems hold fab and test data (MES, FDC, SPC, YMS, test data)?
Which data standards apply (SEMI E5/E30/E37/E142, STDF, RITdb)?
What data do foundries and OSATs share with customers and how?
Who are the main software vendors?
title: Manufacturing and test data: MES, FDC, yield management, test data standards and cross-company sharing
why_it_matters: Yield drives cost; manufacturing and test data are generated at every step but reportedly shared only partially across foundry, OSAT and fabless boundaries.

questions: Which firms provide interposers, substrates, HBM and assembly for AI accelerators?
What are the capacity bottlenecks (interposer, substrate, HBM, hybrid bonders)?
Where is the boundary between foundry and OSAT in advanced packaging?
What equipment is specific to advanced packaging?
title: Advanced packaging and HBM supply chain: CoWoS-class 2.5D, hybrid bonding, substrates and OSAT roles
why_it_matters: AI accelerators depend on 2.5D/3D packaging and HBM; capacity and know-how are concentrated in Asia and a few firms.

questions: What share of layers use EUV vs DUV by node?
Who supplies EUV subsystems (optics, sources, pellicles, mask blanks, resists)?
What are High-NA adoption plans by chipmaker?
What export controls apply to lithography tools?
title: Lithography and critical equipment dependencies: EUV/High-NA, masks, resists and the equipment supplier base
why_it_matters: Leading-edge manufacturing depends on a sole EUV supplier and a narrow optics, source, mask and resist supply base.

questions: What is each leading chipmaker's node roadmap and transistor architecture?
How are memory makers scaling DRAM and NAND?
How fast are SiC and GaN power devices moving to larger wafers?
What does IRDS say about roadmap limits?
title: Process technology roadmap and transitions: GAA, backside power, 3D DRAM/NAND, wide-bandgap (SiC/GaN)
why_it_matters: Transistor and material transitions change which equipment, EDA capabilities and materials are needed, and which firms win.

questions: How are forecasts and orders exchanged between OEMs, Tier-1s, distributors, fabless firms, foundries and OSATs?
What contract forms (LTAs, capacity reservation, take-or-pay) exist?
What visibility tools or data-sharing initiatives exist (government or industry)?
title: Demand forecasting, allocation and supply-chain visibility between chip suppliers and customers
why_it_matters: The 2021 shortage showed inventories fell to under 5 days and firms do not share demand information; how forecasts, orders and allocation flow is unclear.

questions: How is design IP protected across EDA, foundry, mask shop and OSAT?
What do DMEA trusted accreditation and similar schemes require?
Which export controls cover EDA, IP and design data?
What hardware security standards exist?
title: Security, IP protection and trusted supply chain: design-data confidentiality, trusted suppliers and export controls on design tools
why_it_matters: Design data and PDKs are highly sensitive; defense programs require accredited trusted suppliers and the US controls EDA exports for GAAFET design.

why_it_matters: SIA/BCG flag photoresist, specialty gases and wafers as chokepoints and SEMI sizes materials at USD 73bn, but firm-level shares and qualification lock-in are not yet evidenced.

why_it_matters: Equipment is a USD 135bn market with single-supplier points (EUV) and a large post-sale service pool (~25% of ASML sales) that matter for both chokepoint and opportunity analysis.

primary_sources: Avnet, Arrow, WPG, WT Microelectronics annual reports
US DoD / GAO counterfeit parts reports
questions: What share of chip sales goes through distribution vs direct?

why_it_matters: Distributors sit between chipmakers and tens of thousands of OEM/EMS buyers, and the open-market broker channel is where counterfeits enter; the size of each channel is unknown.

Broadcom, Marvell, GUC, Alchip annual reports
